as_told.title: Bahnson and Wheeler set up Bryce DeWitt at the UNC Institute of Field Physics for anti-gravity
as_told.place_text: University of North Carolina, Chapel Hill

plain: A researcher named Eric Weinstein, speaking on a podcast hosted by Jesse Michels, tells of a wealthy man named Agnew Bahnson who, in the 1950s, approached a physicist named Bryce DeWitt and asked him to found an institute at the University of North Carolina at Chapel Hill. In his first telling Weinstein was unsure of the man's name and said the money came from tobacco or air conditioning. In a later telling he says Bahnson and another physicist, John Wheeler, sought DeWitt out together and set him up at what was called the Institute of Field Physics. Weinstein says its purpose was anti-gravity, and he points to an old newspaper clipping. Michels repeats the story in his own words on other episodes, calling Bahnson an industrialist. He ties the institute to a 1957 conference at Chapel Hill and to famous physicists such as Richard Feynman, Peter Bergmann, Freeman Dyson and Wheeler, and he says the work there often dealt with gravitational anomalies, meaning strange behaviour of gravity. The two tell it because, if true, private money was quietly backing research into controlling gravity as early as the 1950s.
